# Homework 9

## Introduction

## Reading in the Data

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)

# read in data
# use 'Latin1' for locale 
bike_data <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale = locale(encoding = "Latin1"))
```

## Checking the Data (EDA)

```{r}
# check for any missing values (#1)
colSums(is.na(bike_data))

# check structure (#2) ; (can also use 'glimpse' which has a nicer output)
str(bike_data)
glimpse(bike_data)

# convert 'Date' column from chr into actual dates (day/month/year) & confirm change (#3) 
bike_data$Date <- dmy(trimws(bike_data$Date))
glimpse(bike_data)

# take a look at data itself
head(bike_data)

# do summary stats for numeric columns (#2)
summary(bike_data)

# check unique values for categorical variables (#2)
unique(bike_data$Seasons)
unique(bike_data$Holiday)
unique(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# turn character variables into factors (Seasons, Holiday, Functioning Day) and check levels (#4)

bike_data$Seasons <- factor(bike_data$Seasons)
levels(bike_data$Seasons)

bike_data$Holiday <- factor(bike_data$Holiday)
levels(bike_data$Holiday)

bike_data$`Functioning Day` <- factor(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
levels(bike_data$`Functioning Day`)

# double check to make sure structure looks good, specifically for date and factors w/ levels 
str(bike_data)

# rename all variables for easier use & confirm change (#5)
names(bike_data)

bike_data <- bike_data |>
  rename(
    date = Date,
    bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`,
    hour = Hour,
    temp = `Temperature(°C)`,
    humidity = `Humidity(%)`,
    wind_speed = `Wind speed (m/s)`,
    visibility = `Visibility (10m)`,
    dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`,
    solar_radiation = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`,
    rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`,
    snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`,
    seasons = Seasons,
    holiday = Holiday,
    functioning_day = `Functioning Day`
  )

names(bike_data)

# create summary statistics for numeric variables (#6)
bike_data |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# create summary statistics for categorical variables using bike rental count (#6)  

# by season
bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by functioning day
bike_data |>
  group_by(functioning_day) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# exclude non-functioning observations since rentals won't happen on those days (#6)
bike_data <- bike_data |>
  filter(functioning_day == "Yes")

# summarize across hours so each day has one observation (#7)
daily_bike <- bike_data |>
  # group by date, seasons, and holiday
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  
  # find sum of bike_count, rainfall, & snowfall
  summarise(
    bike_count = sum(bike_count),
    rainfall = sum(rainfall),
    snowfall = sum(snowfall),
    
    # find mean of other weather-related variables
    temp = mean(temp),
    humidity = mean(humidity),
    wind_speed = mean(wind_speed),
    visibility = mean(visibility),
    dew_point_temp = mean(dew_point_temp),
    solar_radiation = mean(solar_radiation),
    
    .groups = "drop" # removes grouping
  )

# check new dataset 
glimpse(daily_bike)

# recreate basic summary stats (#8) 

# numeric variables
daily_bike |>
  select(
    where(is.numeric)
    ) |>
  summary()

# categorical variables   

# by season
daily_bike |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# by holiday
daily_bike |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarise(
    mean_rentals = mean(bike_count),
    median_rentals = median(bike_count),
    sd_rentals = sd(bike_count),
    total_rentals = sum(bike_count),
    min_rentals = min(bike_count),
    max_rentals = max(bike_count),
    count = n()
  )

# create plots to explore relationships (#8)

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across seasons
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = seasons, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Season",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) + 
  theme_grey()

# boxplot: compare daily bike rentals across holidays and non-holidays
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = holiday, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Daily Bike Rentals by Holiday",
    x = "Holiday (Y/N)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# scatterplot: compare daily bike rentals across temperature 
ggplot(
  daily_bike, 
  aes(
    x = temp, 
    y = bike_count
    )) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm"
    ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bike Rentals vs. Temperature",
    x = "Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Number of Daily Bike Rentals"
  ) +
  theme_grey()

# report correlation between numeric variables (#8)
daily_bike |>
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs") |>
  round(2) |>
  as.data.frame() |> # nicer to look at than a matrix, to me personally

```

## Splitting the Data (1st)

```{r}
# set seed for reproduction
set.seed(13)

# split data into training and test set (75/25 split) & use 'strata' to stratify the split on 'seasons'
split_bike <- initial_split(
  daily_bike,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

train_bike <- training(split_bike)
test_bike <- testing(split_bike)

# check number of observations for 75/25 split
nrow(train_bike)
nrow(test_bike)
```

## Fitting a MLR Model (1st)

```{r}
# create weekday/weekend variable in training data
train_bike <- train_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
      wday(
        date, 
        week_start = 1
        ) %in% c(6, 7),
      "Weekend",
      "Weekday"
    ), 
    levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# create weekday/weekend variable in testing data
test_bike <- test_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
      wday(
        date, 
        week_start = 1
        ) %in% c(6, 7),
      "Weekend",
      "Weekday"
    ),
    levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# check for new variable
str(train_bike)
str(test_bike)
table(train_bike$day_type)
table(test_bike$day_type)

# create standardized versions of numeric variables 

num_vars <- c(
  "temp", "humidity", "wind_speed", "visibility",
  "dew_point_temp", "solar_radiation", "rainfall", "snowfall"
)

# calculate means using training data
train_means <- sapply(train_bike[num_vars], mean)

# calculate standard deviations using training data
train_sds <- sapply(train_bike[num_vars], sd)

# check
train_means
train_sds

# standardize training data using the training means and sds
train_bike <- train_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - train_means[[cur_column()]]) / train_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# standardize testing data using the training means and sds
test_bike <- test_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - train_means[[cur_column()]]) / train_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# fit a model with all the standardized numeric variables included along with the seasons, holiday, and weekend/weekday variables
model1 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type,
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model1)

# fit a model with all the terms in the first model but also interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and temp, and temp and rainfall

model2 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall,
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model2)

# fit a model with all the terms in the second model and also squared terms for the temp and humidity variables (standardized versions)
# use I() to create the quadratic terms

model3 <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall +
    I(temp^2) + 
    I(humidity^2),
  data = train_bike
)

summary(model3)

# predict daily bike rentals for each model using test data
pred1 <- predict(model1, newdata = test_bike)
pred2 <- predict(model2, newdata = test_bike)
pred3 <- predict(model3, newdata = test_bike)

# find test set RMSE for each model 
rmse1 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred1)^2))
rmse2 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred2)^2))
rmse3 <- sqrt(mean((test_bike$bike_count - pred3)^2))

# compare RMSE values
rmse_results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3"),
  RMSE = c(rmse1, rmse2, rmse3)
)

# display results (from lowest to highest RMSE) & determine which model minimizes this test set RMSE
rmse_results |>
  arrange(RMSE)
# model 3 has the lowest RMSE

# create weekday/weekend variable for the entire data set
full_bike <- daily_bike |>
  mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        wday(
          date, 
          week_start = 1
          ) %in% c(6, 7),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      ),
      levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend")
    )
  )

# check for new variable
str(full_bike)
table(full_bike$day_type)

# calculate means and sds using the full dataset
full_means <- sapply(full_bike[num_vars], mean)
full_sds <- sapply(full_bike[num_vars], sd)

# check 
full_means
full_sds

# standardize numeric predictors using the full dataset
full_bike <- full_bike |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(num_vars),
      ~ (.x - full_means[[cur_column()]]) / full_sds[[cur_column()]]
    )
  )

# fit model 3 using full dataset 
final_model <- lm(
  bike_count ~ 
    temp + 
    humidity + 
    wind_speed + 
    visibility +
    dew_point_temp + 
    solar_radiation + 
    rainfall + 
    snowfall +
    seasons + 
    holiday + 
    day_type +
    seasons:holiday + 
    seasons:temp + 
    temp:rainfall +
    I(temp^2) + 
    I(humidity^2),
  data = train_bike
)
```

# Homework 10
```{r}
library(tidymodels)
```

## Splitting the Data (2nd)

```{r}
# set seed for reproduction
set.seed(18)

# split data into training and test sets (75/25) & use 'strata' to stratify the split on 'seasons'
split_bike <- initial_split(
  daily_bike,
  prop = 0.75,
  strata = seasons
)

# create training & test datasets
train_bike <- training(split_bike)
test_bike <- testing(split_bike)

# check number of observations for 75/25 split
nrow(train_bike)
nrow(test_bike)

# create 10-fold cross-validation split using training data
set.seed(21)

bike_folds <- vfold_cv(
  train_bike,
  v = 10
)

# display
bike_folds
```

## Fitting the MLR Models (2nd)
Recipes tell R to perform certain preprocessing steps before fitting a model.

### Recipe 1
```{r}
# create the first recipe
bike_rec1 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ .,
  data = train_bike
) |>
  
  # extract day of the week from date
  step_date(
    date, 
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  
  # create weekday/weekend variable
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  
  # remove original date & intermediate date variable
  step_rm(date, date_dow) |>
  
  # standardize numeric predictors
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  
  # create dummy variables for categorical predictors 
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type)

bike_rec1
```

### Recipe 2
```{r}
# create the second recipe
bike_rec2 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ ., 
  data = train_bike
) |>
  
  step_date(
    date,
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  
  step_rm(date, date_dow) |>
  
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  
  # create interaction terms
  # `starts_with()` selects the new dummy variables with a common prefix
  step_interact(
    terms = ~
      
      # interaction between seasons and holiday
      starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") + 
      
      # interaction between seasons and temp
      starts_with("seasons_"):temp +
      
      # interaction between temp and rainfall
      temp:rainfall
  )

bike_rec2
```

### Recipe 3
```{r}
# create the third recipe
bike_rec3 <- recipe(
  bike_count ~ ., 
  data = train_bike
) |>
  
  step_date(
    date,
    features = "dow"
  ) |>
  
  step_mutate(
    day_type = factor(
      if_else(
        date_dow %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
        "Weekend",
        "Weekday"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  
  step_rm(date, date_dow) |>
  
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  
  step_dummy(seasons, holiday, day_type) |>
  
  step_interact(
    terms = ~
      starts_with("seasons_"):starts_with("holiday_") + 
      starts_with("seasons_"):temp +
      temp:rainfall
  ) |>
  
  # create (standardized) quadratic terms
  step_mutate(
    temp_squared = temp^2,
    hum_squared = humidity^2
  )

bike_rec3
```

### Fitting the 3 MLR Models

- `workflows` connects each recipe with the lm model. 

```{r}
# specify the linear regression model
lm_model <- linear_reg() |>
  set_engine("lm")

# create workflow for each models
bike_wkf1 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec1) |>
  add_model(lm_model)
bike_wkf1

bike_wkf2 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec2) |>
  add_model(lm_model)
bike_wkf2

bike_wkf3 <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec3) |>
  add_model(lm_model)
bike_wkf3
```

- `fit_resamples()` evaluates each workflow using the same 10 folds. 

```{r}
# fit model 1 using cross-validation
bike_fit1 <- bike_wkf1 |>
  fit_resamples(bike_folds)

# fit model 2 using CV
bike_fit2 <- bike_wkf2 |>
  fit_resamples(bike_folds)

# fit model 3 using CV
bike_fit3 <- bike_wkf3 |>
  fit_resamples(bike_folds)
```

### Comparing the 3 MLR Models
```{r}
# combine & collect CV RMSE results 
rbind(
  bike_fit1 |> 
    collect_metrics() |>
    filter(.metric == "rmse"),
  
  bike_fit2 |> 
    collect_metrics() |>
    filter(.metric == "rmse"),
  
  bike_fit3 |> 
    collect_metrics() |>
    filter(.metric == "rmse")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3")
    ) |>
  select(Model, RMSE = mean, n, std_err) |>
  arrange(RMSE)
```
Model 2 has lowest RMSE, so it is the best-performing MLR model (based on CV).

### Fitting the Best MLR Model 

- `last_fit()` fits the model on the entire training data set & evaluates its performance on the test data set. 

```{r}
# fit the best model to the entire training data set
final_lm <- bike_wkf2 |>
  last_fit(split_bike)

# examine test data set performance 
final_lm |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  select(
    .metric,
    .estimator,
    .estimate
  )
```


## Fitting Other Models

### (Tuned) Regression Tree Model
A **regression tree** divides the data into groups based on predictor values and makes predictions within those groups. 

```{r}
# set up the regression tree model 

# use `tune()` bc we don't know which values will produce the best regression tree
# aka tell tidymodels to test different values and determine which combo works best 

tree_model <- decision_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune(),
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# create workflow to combine the first recipe with the regression tree model 
tree_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec1) |>
  add_model(tree_model)

# tune the regression tree using 10-fold CV
set.seed(13)

tree_tune <- tree_wkf |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = 10
  )

# examine tuning results
tree_tune |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)

# select the best model based on RMSE
best_tree <- select_best(
  tree_tune, 
  metric = "rmse")
best_tree

# finalize workflow with the best parameters 
fin_tree_wkf <- tree_wkf |>
  finalize_workflow(best_tree)

# fit to the entire training data set
fin_tree_fit <- fin_tree_wkf |>
  last_fit(split_bike)
fin_tree_fit

# examine test data set performance 
fin_tree_fit |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  select(
    .metric, 
    .estimator,
    .estimate
  )
```

### (Tuned) Bagged Tree Model
A **bagged tree* (aka *bootstrap aggregated decision tree*) fits multiple decision trees to different bootstrap samples of the training data, then combines their predictions. It helps reduce the variability that can come from relying on just one regression tree. 

```{r}
library(baguette)

# set up the bagged tree model
bag_model <-bag_tree(
  cost_complexity = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# create workflow to combine the first recipe with the bagged tree model 
bag_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec1) |>
  add_model(bag_model)

# tune the bagged tree using 10-fold CV
set.seed(18)

bag_tune <- bag_wkf |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = 10
  )

# examine tuning results
bag_tune |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)

# select the best model based on RMSE
best_bag <- select_best(
  bag_tune, 
  metric = "rmse")
best_bag

# finalize workflow with the best parameters 
fin_bag_wkf <- bag_wkf |>
  finalize_workflow(best_bag)

# fit to the entire training data set
fin_bag_fit <- fin_bag_wkf |>
  last_fit(split_bike)
fin_bag_fit

# examine test data set performance 
fin_bag_fit |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  select(
    .metric, 
    .estimator,
    .estimate
  )
```

### (Tuned) Random Forest Model
A **random forest model** combines predictions from multiple decision trees, though at each split it randomly selects a subset of predictors.This makes individual trees less alike. 

```{r}
library(ranger)

# set up the random forest model
rf_model <- rand_forest(
  mtry = tune()
) |>
  set_engine("ranger") |>
  set_mode("regression")

# create workflow to combine the first recipe with the random forest model 
rf_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(bike_rec1) |>
  add_model(rf_model)

# tune the random forest using 10-fold CV
set.seed(21)

rf_tune <- rf_wkf |>
  tune_grid(
    resamples = bike_folds,
    grid = 10
  )

# examine tuning results
rf_tune |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)

# select the best model based on RMSE
best_rf <- select_best(
  rf_tune, 
  metric = "rmse")
best_rf

# finalize workflow with the best parameters 
fin_rf_wkf <- rf_wkf |>
  finalize_workflow(best_rf)

# fit to the entire training data set
fin_rf_fit <- fin_rf_wkf |>
  last_fit(split_bike)
fin_rf_fit

# examine test data set performance 
fin_rf_fit |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  select(
    .metric, 
    .estimator,
    .estimate
  )
```

## Comparing Models on Test Sets
